hard_fail_flags.evidence: In the 'Written for the person who has to approve it' section, the aside reads: 'For the sales engineer waiting on all this: a draft that arrives already checked gets approved in one pass instead of three. The speed comes from fewer rounds, not from skipping the review.' This is a quantified review-round/time-saving claim stated as fact; the brief says there are no accuracy or time-saved numbers, and the page itself later says 'we don't have accuracy or time-saved figures we'd put on a page'.
hard_fail_flags.steps: Open packets/P008/B/index.html from disk at 1440x900; scroll to #review; read the paragraph with class 'aside-note' below the three points.

reason: As the security lead, A puts a cited answer and a flagged, not-drafted question with quoted sources right beside the headline at 1440, every reviewer control works with a reset, and every claim is either from the brief or explicitly marked unmeasured; as the sales engineer, A gives me my own path and the handoff. B's sentence-level check is excellent, but it is below the fold, its reviewer step auto-approves with a dead Send back, the sales engineer gets one line, and it adds an unsupported 'one pass instead of three' claim. I would change my mind only if A's mobile first screen were judged decisive and B's claim were accepted as framing rather than a number.
